messages:
Sara-CS: FYI customer (FinCloud) says their quantized endpoint is higher latency than FP16 and hallucinating more. opened a ticket with traces and a short repro.
Alex: ugh. can you paste the repro here? which model + seq len + payload?
Sara-CS: model: rdlw-7b-v2 (quantized fp8-int8 mix). seq 1024 prompt + 256 gen. batch=1. curl example in ticket: 
Sara-CS: ```bash
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \u002dH 'Authorization: Bearer <key>' \u002dH 'Content-Type: application/json' \u002d-d '{"model":"rdlw-7b-v2-quant","input":"<long prompt>","max_tokens":256,"stream":false}'
```
Priya: thanks. any perf numbers? p50/p95? GPU util?
Sara-CS: p50 went from ~120ms (fp16) to ~360ms (quant) per token on their workload. p95 spikes to 1.2s. GPU util lower (~35%) vs fp16 (~78%).
Ravi: low GPU util + higher latency suggests inefficient kernel or memory stalls. can we get a profile? nvprof / nsys traces?
Sara-CS: attached flamegraph image in ticket and a .nspy file. I uploaded the small profile here: https://internal/fincloud/rdlw7b-quant.nsys
Alex: downloading. initial glance: kernel selector picked `int8_matmul_v2` on a few layers but fell back to a smaller `fp8_attention_emulate` path for attention. there's lots of memcpy/syncs around KV cache step.
Priya: is KV cache disabled or getting serialized per request? customer mentioned they use streaming=false but do many short generate calls.
Sara-CS: they said streaming false, they do repeated single-turn requests in a loop (per-chat UI).
Ravi: that pattern kills quantized runtimes if our KV path isn't optimized. quant kernels assume contiguous KV cache layout; if we rehydrate KV per-call with CPU memcpy it's expensive.
Alex: exact spot in trace: 
Alex: ```
# simplified trace lines
int8_matmul_v2     0.28ms  (good)
fp8_attention_emulate  1.6ms (per layer)
kv_rehydrate_cpu_memcpy 0.9ms x num_layers
sync_cuda  0.5ms x many
```
Alex: on long seq (1024) attention emulation cost multiplies and memcpy churn dominates.
Priya: also note batch=1. our batching heuristic currently prefers quant kernels for cost but doesn't consider seq_len threshold. we should prefer fp16 for seq > 512 or small batch sizes.
Sara-CS: customer asks for immediate mitigation while you fix runtime. any config we can recommend?
Ravi: two immediate mitigations: 1) set runtime hint to `prefer_fp16=true` for that model endpoint (forces kernel router to pick fp16 path). 2) enable `kv_pinned_memory=true` so KV stays GPU-resident between calls (if they're doing many calls from same connection). both are quick config flips.
Priya: config example to send: 
Priya: ```json
{
  "model": "rdlw-7b-v2-quant",
  "endpoint_config": {
    "kernel_routing": { "force_fp16": true },
    "kv": { "persistent_on_connection": true, "kv_pinned_memory": true }
  }
}
```
Alex: note: `force_fp16` forces FP16 kernels even if weights are quantized; perf penalty on throughput in ideal large-batch cases but good p50 for single-turn.
Sara-CS: I'll send that to customer and offer temporary flip. anything else to note about quality? they said hallucinations increased on quant.
Ravi: quant calibration can change generation quality. if they care about fidelity, recommend re-calibrating with representative prompts or use `quant_calibration=dynamic` which re-computes scales per-batch at slight perf cost. but for immediate safety, FP16 avoids calibration drift.
Priya: longer-term fixes: we should update kernel selector to consider seq_len and kv_rehydration_cost. also add a fast-path attention kernel for mixed precision with prepacked KV to avoid per-call memcpy.
Alex: agree. propose change: if seq_len>512 OR batch_size<=2 -> prefer fp16; else keep current cost model. Ravi can own perf tests.
Ravi: I can run microbenchmarks on rdlw-7b variants tomorrow and iterate. I'll also test an optimized KV layout change that reduces memcpy calls by coalescing per-layer KV into a single buffer.
Sara-CS: customer accepted temp `force_fp16` flip, asking ETA on runtime fix. any rough timeline?
Priya: hotfix for kernel routing heuristics could be a 1-week patch (tests + rollout). KV layout change is larger — 3-4 weeks with verification.
Alex: assignable items: 
Alex: - Ravi: perf microbench + KV layout prototype (owner).
Alex: - Priya: draft runtime config toggle and rollback plan (owner).
Alex: - Sara-CS: notify customer and coordinate FP16 flip, collect any updated traces after flip (owner).
deploy-bot: deploy request queued: patch-avoid-quant-smallbatch (dry run) by Priya.
Sara-CS: noted. I'll schedule the flip for their non-prod endpoint now and ask for updated p50/p95 within 24h. will update ticket. thanks all. :thumbsup:
